items.text: At the start of 2019, China did something that no other space program has ever done – it landed a spacecraft on the surface of the far side of the moon. The reason people sent spacecraft to the near side is because spacecraft need to face Earth in order to establish a direct radio link with ground control . Chinese scientists got around this by sending a satellite around 64,000 kilometres beyond the moon. This satellite will constantly send a signal between Earth and the spacecraft on the moon. The Chinese rover will explore the lunar surface using a series of scientific instruments to study one of the moon’s largest and oldest craters. Scientists hope to find and study material from the deep lunar crater to see if the information can help us understand the moon’s evolution, as well as how the crater was formed. Also, because the far side of the moon is hidden from Earth’s radio noise , this could be an excellent place to perform clear radio astronomy. Difficult words: establish (create), ground control (the people on Earth who control the spacecraft), get around (solve), rover (a vehicle which drives over rough terrain), radio noise (radio signals from Earth), perform (do). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

At the start of 2019, China landed a spacecraft on the far side of the moon. Nobody did this in the past. People only sent spacecraft to the near side of the moon because spacecraft need to face Earth if they want to communicate with us. Chinese scientists found a solution for this. They sent a satellite 64,000 kilometres behind the moon. This satellite will send information between Earth and the spacecraft on the moon. There will be a car which will go on the moon’s surface. The car will visit one of the moon’s largest and oldest craters . Scientists hope to find and study material from the deep moon’s crater. They want to understand the moon’s evolution better. They want to understand how the crater was formed. Difficult words: spacecraft (a vehicle which can travel in space), face (see), crater (space in the ground). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

China sends a spacecraft to the moon. It does this at the start of 2019. It sends the spacecraft to the far side of the moon. The spacecraft is the first spacecraft to go to the far side. People usually only send spacecraft to the near side. This is because there must be communication between Earth and the spacecraft. China solves this problem. There is another spacecraft behind the moon. The spacecraft on the moon and people from Earth send information to it. This is how the spacecraft communicates with the Earth. China wants to study a crater of the moon. It is one of the biggest and oldest craters. It can tell us about the moon’s evolution . Difficult words: spacecraft (a machine which can travel in space), solve (understand a problem and make it go away), crater (a space in the ground), evolution (how something changes to how it is now). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Jair Bolsonaro was sworn in as Brazil’s next president on last Tuesday, and he made some pretty substantial promises in his inaugural speech . He promised to create a ‘society without discrimination or division ’ and he said that he would ‘free the country from corruption and crime’. Jair Bolsonaro is a former army captain and he has stacked his cabinet with military leaders, some of whom have little to no political experience. Some Brazilians have even expressed fears that he could bring back military rule to the country. People also criticised him for making controversial comments about homosexuality, black people and women. The American president, Donald Trump, congratulated Bolsonaro on Twitter, saying, ‘The USA is with you!’ Difficult words: substantial (huge), inaugural speech (the speech you give when you start an important job), division (a separation of people into two or more groups), former (-ex), stack (fill in a certain way), controversial (something controversialmakes people talkand argue because they feel strongly about it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Jair Bolsonaro was sworn in as Brazil’s next president on last Tuesday. In his speech, he made some pretty big promises. He promised to create a ‘society without discrimination or division ’ and he also said that he would free the country from ‘corruption and crime’. Jair Bolsonaro is a former army captain, and he filled his cabinet with military leaders. Some Brazilians fear that he could bring military rule back to the country. People also criticised him for his comments about homosexuality, black people and women. The American president, Donald Trump, congratulated Bolsonaro on Twitter. Difficult words: swear in (officially say that somebody is the president), division (a separation of people into two or more groups), former (-ex), cabinet (a group of people that a president chooses to help him or her). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Jair Bolsonaro becomes Brazil’s new president. He gives a speech. He makes big promises . He says that he is going to end crime and corruption. He also wants to unite the people. Jair Bolsonaro is an ex-army captain. His ‘co-workers’ are also from the army. Some people do not like this. People also criticise him for his comments about homosexuality, black people and women. The American president, Donald Trump, congratulates Bolsonaro on Twitter. Difficult words: promise (saying that you are going to do something), be going to (to do something in the future), unite (bring together). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At least four people have died after a suspected gas explosion caused part of an apartment building to collapse in southern Russia last Monday. The governor of the region where the incident took place said that 8 of the 120 residents who live in the 10-story building in are missing. Reuters reported that gas explosions occur frequently in Russia, where older buildings have not undergone the latest infrastructure updates and are not outfitted with the necessary safety requirements. The apartment building complex where this explosion happened was reportedly built in 1973. Difficult words: suspected (people are unsure what happened), Reuters (a large news agency), infrastructure (the work needed to build a city and its resources), reportedly (according to what some say – it may not be completely true). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last Monday, there was a suspected gas explosion at an apartment building in southern Russia. Part of the building collapsed and at least four people died. Eight of the 120 residents who live in the 10-story building were missing after the incident. Gas explosions often happen in Russia because the buildings are old, and they do not meet safety requirements . People say that the apartment building where this explosion happened was built in 1973. Difficult words: suspected (people are not sure what happened), collapse (fall down), resident (a person who resides – lives somewhere), safety requirements (rules that make a place or a situation be safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from southern Russia. There is an explosion. It probably is a gas explosion. The explosion happens at a building. One hundred and twenty people live there. At least four people die. Eight people are missing . Gas explosions happen often in Russia. The buildings there are old. They do not meet safety requirements . Difficult words: be missing (when you are missing, people do not know if you are OK and where you are), safety requirements (rules that make a place be safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Vietnamese National Assembly passed a controversial cybersecurity law which took effect on January 1st. The new law requires a number of things. For example, big tech companies such as Facebook have to store local user data in Vietnam, provide information to the government (if asked), and remove any content deemed offensive or harmful. Foreign tech firms serving more than 10,000 Vietnamese users must also establish offices in Vietnam. Some people have criticised the law, saying that it will lead to further government crackdowns on the opposition and hamper free speech in the country. The country’s government, on the other hand, says that the law is necessary to combat cybercrime and to protect users’ information. Those to whom the law applies have a year to comply with the requirements, but tech companies and rights groups objected to the law, and US lawmakers even wrote a letter to Facebook and to Google asking them not to comply. Difficult words: assembly (a group of people who make laws in a country), controversial (people talk about controversial problems or argue because they feel strongly about the problems), deem (regard as, think of as), crackdown (repression), hamper (block), comply (meet the standards). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A new cybersecurity law in Vietnam took effect on January 1st. Tech companies have a year to comply to everything that the law says. For example Facebook has to store user data in Vietnam, must provide information to the government (if the government asks for it), and must remove certain content if the government orders it. Foreign tech companies in Vietnam that have more than 10,000 Vietnamese users must have offices in Vietnam. Some people criticise the law. They say that it gives the government too much power and that it is not good for free speech. The government, on the other hand, says that the law protects people’s information and helps fight cybercrime. It is interesting that the American government wrote to Facebook and Google and asked not to comply to the new law. Difficult words: comply (follow a rule or orders), store (have on servers), government (the ‘bosses’ of a country), content (text, picture or videos on Facebook). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Vietnam, there is a new law. It starts this year. It affects tech companies. Facebook must have user information on servers in Vietnam. If the Vietnamese government wants information from Facebook, Facebook must give the information. If the government wants to delete something from Facebook, Facebook must delete it. The Vietnamese government says that the law protects people’s information. It also says that this can fight cybercrime. Some people criticise the new law. They say that it is not good for free speech. They also say that it gives the government too much power. It is interesting that the American government writes to Facebook and to Google. It asks them not to comply to the new law. Difficult words: affect (changes, makes them make changes), government (the ‘bosses’ of a country), comply (follow a rule). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Monarch butterflies have the important job of pollination , but their worldwide population is falling. In California, an organisation found that there were very few monarch butterflies visiting in the 2018 winter so far. The organisation found an 86% decline in the number of butterflies that people observed. However, the organisation counts for several weeks, so people are still sending in data. Worldwide, the population of all butterflies fell by 0.05 per cent. Researchers think that habitat loss and pesticides may have contributed , and by fixing these problems and by increasing conservation, people can help the butterflies. Difficult words: pollination (spreading flower pollen to other flowers to make more plants), decline (a fall), habitat (an animal’s natural home), pesticide (a chemical that people use to kill insects), contribute (add up to a problem). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Monarch butterflies are important pollinators , but their global population is falling. In California, an organisation found that there were very few monarch butterflies visiting during this 2018 winter. There was an 86% fall in the number of butterflies that they saw. Around the world, the population for all butterflies fell by 0.05 percent. Scientists think that habitat loss and pesticides probably caused this. By fixing these problems and doing more conservation work, people can help the butterflies. Difficult words: pollinator (an insect that spreads pollen so flowers and plants can grow), habitat loss (losing the animal’s natural home), pesticide (a chemical that people put on plants to kill insects), conservation (protection of animals or plants). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Monarch butterflies are important. They move pollen from flowers to other flowers. Pollen is the yellow dust you can see in flowers. This makes flowers and plants grow. However, there are fewer monarch butterflies now. An organisation counts butterflies in California. People do this in the winter. They find that there are 86% less butterflies in 2018. Around the world, there are less butterflies, too. Scientists think that two problems hurt them. The problems are habitat loss and pesticides . People need to fix these problems. They need to do more conservation . Then, people can help the butterflies. Difficult words: habitat loss (when an animal or plant loses its natural home), pesticide (a thing that people put on plants to kill insects), conservation (protecting animals or plants). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

According to Operation Inherent Resolve, which is the US military’s name for the military intervention against ISIS in Syria and Iraq, the US-led coalition strikes led to the unintentional deaths of at least 1,139 civilians. There were over 31,000 strikes launched between August 2014 and the end of November 2018, and the operation freed nearly 8 million Iraqis and Syrians from ISIS rule. The ISIS-controlled territory reduced to about 1 per cent of what the group had before. However, Airwars, a non-profit company monitoring civilian harm from air strikes, reports that the number of civilian deaths from US-led coalition actions in Iraq and Syria could be as high as 11,637. That number could still be higher because the agency counts deaths which were deemed confirmed or fair. Difficult words: intervention (intervening – getting into someone else’s fight), strike (air strike), unintentional (not done on purpose, not wanted), launch (start), harm (danger), coalition (a collection of groups), deem (think to be the case), confirmed (something confirmed happened for sure). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

According to the US military , the air strikes against ISIS in Syria and Iraq led to the unintentional deaths of at least 1,139 civilians . There were over 31,000 air strikes between August 2014 and the end of November 2018. The US report also says that the operation freed nearly 8 million Iraqis and Syrians from ISIS rule. The ISIS-controlled territory reduced to about 1 per cent of what the group had before. However, A non-profit company which monitors civilian deaths, says that the number of deaths is 11,637 or possibly even higher. Difficult words: military (the army), unintentional (not done on purpose, not wanted), civilian (an ordinary person who does not fight). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The USA fights in Syria and Iraq from August 2014 to November 2018. It fights ISIS with air strikes . There are 31,000 strikes in four years. The US military puts a report online. It says that 8 million Iraqis and Syrians are saved from ISIS. The area of ISIS gets very small. However, many civilians die in the air strikes. The US military says that 1,139 civilians die. A non-profit company says that 11,637 or more civilians die. Difficult words: air strike (drop bombs from a plane), military (soldiers), report (a document which tells people about something), civilian (a normal person who does not fight). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Thailand’s lawmakers gave the country’s citizens a special New Year’s gift – a change in an existing law to allow marijuana for medical and research purposes. However, licenses to produce and sell marijuana products will be strictly controlled, and people will be able to carry certain amounts of the drugs if they have a prescription or certificate. The new law also allows kratom, a plant native to the region, which is used to treat pain, anxiety and other issues. South east Asia is known for its strict drug laws and harsh penalties and Thailand is the first country in the region to legalise pot in any way. Marijuana for medicinal and recreational purposes is gaining popularity around the world, but Canada has recently become only the second country to legalise it for recreational use. Difficult words: anxiety (a nervous disorder when you are extremely nervous and can have panic attacks), penalty (punishment for doing something illegal), pot informal (marijuana), recreational (fun). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Marijuana is gaining popularity around the world, and Thailand became the first south east Asian country to legalise it. Beginning with the new year, people will be able to use it as a medicine or study it. However, licenses to produce and sell marijuana products will be strictly controlled. People will be able to carry certain amounts of the drugs if they have a prescription or certificate. The new law also allows kratom, which is a plant native to the region. People use it to treat pain, anxiety and other problems. Difficult words: gain (get), legalise (make legal, you can buy/do legal things and must do buy/do illegal things), anxiety (a medical problem when you are extremely nervous and have panic attacks). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Marijuana is legal in some countries. It is illegal in others. For example, it is illegal in south east Asian countries. However, Thailand changes this. It becomes the first south east Asian country to make marijuana legal. People can sell it and buy it. They can use it as medicine. The Thai government controls, who sells marijuana. You can use it. However, you must have a certificate . Difficult words: legal (you can do/buy legal things), illegal (you must not do/buy illegal things), government (the ‘bosses’ of a country), certificate (a paper that says what you are allowed to do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The officials of North and South Korea participated in a ceremony to connect the countries’ roads and railways. Two trains started from either side of the peninsula and met up at the border. The event was mostly symbolic, but it is another move toward peace. It is not likely much more will happen while North Korea is under international sanctions over its nuclear programme. South Korea had to get an exemption from the UN just to hold the ceremony. Still, South Korea believes that the move shows that both countries are willing to cooperate for rail and roadway modernisation in the future. South Korea’s Unification Ministry said the construction will move forward ‘while observing North Korea’s denuclearisation progress and international sanctions against North Korea. Difficult words: peninsula (a piece of land almost surrounded by water), exemption (an exception, a special change), be willing to do something (when you are willing to do something, you are not very happy about doing it but you do it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There was a ceremony in which South and North Korean roads and railways were connected . The event was symbolic, but it is another step toward peace. South Korea believes that this shows that the countries are willing to work together on rail and road modernisation. North Korea is under international sanctions over its nuclear programme. South Korea said that the construction will go on while North Korea is closely watched. Difficult words: connect (join, become one), be willing to do something (when you are willing to do something, you are not very happy about doing it but you do it anyway), sanctions (a type of punishment that a country can do to another country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

South and North Korea hold an event. It is at the border . Roads and railways are connected at the ceremony. The ceremony is symbolic . We do not know if things can get better. However, this is a good sign . Difficult words: border (the line where two countries meet), connect (join, become one), symbolic (based on an idea), sign (a thing which can mean that something will happen in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The eruption of Anak Krakatau, a volcanic island in Indonesia, triggered an underwater landslide which then caused a tsunami. At least 420 people are confirmed dead, 154 people reported missing, and 1,400 people injured after the tsunami hit on Saturday 22nd. More than 16,000 people were displaced and over 800 homes were destroyed. People have been warned that even more tsunamis could soon strike because of the undersea volcano’s high activity. Difficult words: trigger (cause, make happen), confirm (prove that something is true), displace (forced to leave because of danger or destruction). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Anak Krakatau is a volcanic island in Indonesia which erupted and caused an underwater landslide which then caused a tsunami. The tsumani hit on Saturday 22nd. At least 420 people died, 154 people are missing, and 1,400 people were injured. Over 900 homes were destroyed and 16,000 people had to leave. The undersea volcano is highly active – there could be more tsunamis. Difficult words: erupted (explode), cause (make happen). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Anak Krakatau is a volcanic island. It is in Indonesia. It erupts . It causes an underwater landslide . The landslide makes a tsunami. The tsunami hits on Saturday 22nd. At least 420 people die. Around 150 people are missing. We do not know if they are OK or where they are. Around 1,400 people are injured. Over 900 homes are destroyed. Around 16,000 people must leave because of danger. Difficult words: volcanic (made by a volcano), erupt (explode and start being active), cause (make happen), landslide (when a lot of earth moves). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Taiwan, protesters were taking to the streets for a tax reform for the 3 rd time in seven days with thousands of people gathering in Taipei. An activist group called the Tax and Legal Reform League organised the protests. The group has been working on this issue for years, and the ‘yellow vest’ protests in France inspired it to try again. The French protests stopped the government from raising a gas tax until 2020, and the government also increased minimum wages and other economic reforms . People in Sweden, Israel, and Belgium also held similar protests. In Taiwan, it is unclear if the protests will change anything. Difficult words: gather (come together), league (an organised group), issue (problem), economic reform (a change to how money is controlled in a country). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Taiwan, thousands of protesters came together for a tax reform for the 3 rd time in seven days. An activist group organised the protests, and its work on tax reform started years ago. The ‘yellow vest’ protests in France inspired the group to try again. The French protests stopped the government from raising a gas tax. People in Sweden, Israel, and Belgium also held similar protests. In Taiwan, it is not known if the protests will change anything. Difficult words: tax reform (a change to taxes – the money you pay to help run a country and its government), activist (a person who wants to make changes in a country), inspire (give someone hope to try to do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Taiwan, thousands of protesters come together. They do this three times in seven days. They are protesting for a tax reform . A group organises the protests. It tries to change taxes in Taiwan for years. The ‘yellow vest’ protests happen in France. These protests give people in Taiwan hope. The French protests stop the government from raising a gas tax. People in Sweden, Israel, and Belgium also have similar protests. People are not sure if there can be changes in Taiwan. Difficult words: tax reform (a change to taxes – the money you pay to help run a country), government (the ‘bosses of a country’), gas tax (extra money on gasoline – the liquid we use to run many things like electricity and cars). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A day after Christmas, President Trump gave his first visit to troops in a war zone when he and First Lady Melania Trump gave a surprise visit to US troops in Iraq. The Trumps spent three hours with the troops to thank them for their service. The president also spoke with reporters about the government shut-down back in the US, and he implied that the shut-down would continue until he gets funding for a Mexico-US border. He added that he has no plans to remove the troops from Iraq. A week ago, he said that he would remove troops from Syria. People believe that when the US leaves, some factions in the Syrian war will fight among themselves. The US is unclear how it will leave Syria and if it will continue to support the war through other means. Difficult words: troops (soldiers), government shut-down (when the government closes until the leaders agree on a problem), imply (suggest), faction (a group). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A day after Christmas, President Trump gave his first visit to troops in a war zone when he and First Lady Melania Trump visited US troops in Iraq. The Trumps spent three hours with them. The president also spoke with reporters about the US government shut-down . He also said that he has no plans to remove the troops from Iraq. Recently he said that he would remove troops from Syria. People believe that when the US leaves, some groups in the war will fight one another. It is not known how the US will leave Syria. Difficult words: troop (a group of soldiers), US government shut-down (when the US government closes until government leaders can agree on a problem), remove (take away from somewhere). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

President Trump gives his first visit to troops in a war zone . Trump and First Lady Melania Trump go to Iraq. They go the day after Christmas. They spend three hours with the troops. The president speaks with reporters. He talks about the US government shut-down . He says US troops will stay in Iraq. A little while ago he says that US troops will leave Syria. People think this means more fighting will happen. The fighting will happen if the American troops leave. Difficult words: troop (soldiers), war zone (where a war is happening), US government shut-down (when the US government closes until people in the government can agree on a problem). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Sao Paolo, Brazil, superhero window cleaners visited a children’s hospital to make some sick patients happy, and they did this by rappelling outside the building and stopping at the windows so the children could see them. The window cleaners made themselves become everyday heroes by donning costumes such as the Flash, Batman, Iron Man, Spider Man, and Super Man. The people in charge of the hospital came up with the idea to do this to commemorate Children’s Day which Brazil celebrates on October 12. Usually, parents give their children presents on this day, but hospital staff wanted to do something more. For the window cleaners and superheroes, it was all in a day’s work! Difficult words: rappel (climb down from the top of something by sliding along a rope), don (wear), commemorate (celebrate), all in a day’s work (something someone does normally). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Sao Paolo, Brazil, a children’s hospital wanted to make the sick patients happy on Children’s Day. In Brazil, this happens on October 12, and usually, parents give their children gifts. The hospital wanted to do something more. The hospital staff asked five window washers to become superheroes for the day. The window washers donned their costumes as the Flash, Batman, Iron Man, Spider Man, and Super Man. The five superheroes then hung outside the building and climbed down, stopping at windows as they dropped so the children could see them. Difficult words: patient (a person who is sick or hurt and needs help from a doctor), staff (people who work somewhere), don (put on). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a children’s hospital in Sao Paolo, Brazil. The hospital wants to cheer up some of its sick patients for Children’s Day. Children’s Day is on October 12. The hospital bosses ask five window cleaners to put on costumes. The costumes make them look like superheroes. They look like the Flash, Batman, Iron Man, Spider Man, and Super Man. The super heroes climb down the side of the hospital. They stop at windows as they climb down. The children get to see them. Difficult words: cheer up (make happy), patient (a person who is sick or hurt and needs help from a doctor), climb (move). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

One German couple pulled out all the stops in their Christmas decorations. From the outside, Thomas and Susanne Jeromin’s house looks normal with a few modest decorations. On the inside, the house is filled to the rafters with over 100 Christmas trees crammed into 105 square metres of space. The trees are adorned in fairy lights, ornaments and around 16,000 baubles . The couple had a small collection at first but it grew rapidly as time went on, making them local celebrities. It takes them 8 weeks to prepare for Christmas, as they start decorating in early October and fill every room except the bedroom. Even the bathroom has a Santa Claus toilet seat. Difficult words: pull out all the stops (do a lot of work), fill to the rafters (fill something up completely), cram (put into a small space), adorn (decorate), bauble (a small decoration). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A German couple decorated the outside of their house with a few simple Christmas decorations. The inside of the house, however, is a very different story! The couple filled their small house with over 100 Christmas trees. They decorated the trees with fairy lights and 16,000 baubles . They did not always have so many trees. In the beginning, they had a small Christmas collection. As time went on, they grew their collection rapidly. It takes them 8 weeks to set everything up and they start decorating in early October. They fill every room except the bedroom. They even have a Santa Claus in their bathroom! Difficult words: fairy lights (small coloured electric lights), bauble (a small Christmas decoration), except (but). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A German couple likes Christmas. They have Christmas decorations . They buy more and more decorations every year. Now they have many decorations. They start decorating in October. They take 8 weeks to set everything up. They put 100 Christmas trees into their small house! They decorate the trees with fairy light s and 16,000 baubles . They even have a Santa Clause in their bathroom! Difficult words: decoration (a thing which makes something beautiful), decorate (to put a decoration on something), fairy lights (small coloured electric lights), bauble (a small Christmas decoration). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

21-12-18 07:00 Starbucks is having trouble with growth, so it is upping its delivery game as it expands its delivery service with Uber Eats. Starbucks also has deliveries through services like DoorDash, GrubHub, and PostMates. Additionally, in some cities, customers have had the option to order by delivery for years. Uber Eats is different in that it is working with Starbucks to make a delivery service called ‘Starbucks Delivers’. It has custom beverages made for delivery with special packaging like spill-proof lids, tamper -proof seals , and insulated containers to keep orders hot or cold. In China, Starbucks is testing the service, and deliveries there usually take 30 minutes or less. In the US, the service will be similar and people will be able to order from Starbucks Delivers or Uber Eats. Difficult words: tamper -proof seal (a type of seal which shows that something has not been opened), seal (a thin piece of plastic), insulated (protected to keep the drink hot or cold). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

21-12-18 07:00 Starbucks is not growing as fast as it wants, so it is expanding its delivery service with Uber Eats. It has deliveries through other services, as well. Uber Eats is different in that it is starting a Starbucks delivery services called ‘Starbucks Delivers’. For example, it has drinks with special packaging like spill – proof lids and insulated containers to keep orders hot or cold. Starbucks is testing the service in China. In the US, people will be able to order from Starbucks Delivers or Uber Eats. Difficult words: expand (grow, make bigger), deliver (bring something to somebody), spill-proof (keep from spilling a liquid), insulated (protected to keep the drink hot or cold). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

21-12-18 07:00 Starbucks is a big company. However, it is not growing quickly. Instead it grows its delivery service . It works with a company called Uber Eats. It also works with other delivery services. Uber Eats helps Starbucks start a new delivery service. It is called Starbucks Delivers. It has special drinks. The drink containers are made for delivery. They are insulated . They do not open easily. Starbucks tries the service in China. It wants to try it in the US soon. Difficult words: delivery service (a service which brings you food which you buy on the internet), insulated (protected to keep the drink hot or cold). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Facebook is apologising for a bug that allowed 1,500 third party apps to be able to get into 6.8 million users’ photos without their permission from September 13 th to 25 th . These photos were not usually accessible . Facebook said that the bug allowed the apps to get to photos that users posted or only uploaded to Facebook without posting them. Facebook said that it keeps the unreleased photos in case the users want to post them later. Facebook said that it will notify all users who were impacted by this issue . This is another privacy problem for the company this year. Ireland investigated the company after a security issue affected many accounts there. This also comes after Facebook admitted that Cambridge Analytica received millions of users’ information without permission. Difficult words: bug (an error that makes a program do something unexpected), third party (a group/person other than the two group/people – Facebook and the user in this case), accessible (able to get to something), impact (affect), notify (send a message), issue (problem). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Facebook is apologising because a bug allowed third party apps to get into millions of users’ photos without their permission in September. Apps could not usually get to these photos. Facebook said that the bug let apps get to the photos that were posted on Facebook or only uploaded. Facebook said that it keeps uploaded photos in case the user wants to post them later. Facebook will tell all users who had this happen to them. This is another privacy problem for the company this year. Difficult words: bug (a problem that makes a program do something that people do not want), third party (a group/person other than the two group/people – Facebook and the user in this case), post (put on Facebook for your Facebook friends to see). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In September, a bug happens in Facebook. It lets other apps get into millions of people’s photos. Apps cannot normally do this. Facebook says that it is sorry.
